sentences.en: At the turn of the 6th century BC, a man called Thales of Miletus did something truly extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 公元前6世纪之交，一位名叫米利都的泰勒斯的人做了一件真正非凡的事情。

sentences.en: He argued that instead of relying on myths and legends, the best way to understand the world
sentences.zh: 他主张，与其依赖神话和传说，了解世界的最佳方式

sentences.en: was through theories and hypotheses drawn from real-world experiments, something we would call science.
sentences.zh: 是通过从现实世界实验中得出的理论和假设，也就是我们所说的科学。

sentences.en: Where Thales led, other Greeks followed.
sentences.zh: 泰勒斯开创了先河，其他希腊人也纷纷效仿。

sentences.en: For centuries, they made spectacular advances in understanding their world, inventing geometry, astronomy, physics and chemistry.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，他们在理解世界方面取得了惊人的进步，发明了几何学、天文学、物理学和化学。

sentences.en: And then came darkness.
sentences.zh: 然后，黑暗降临了。

sentences.en: At the end of the classical age, the world fell back into ignorance and superstition.
sentences.zh: 古典时代末期，世界重新陷入了无知和迷信之中。

sentences.en: People lived like dogs in the gutter.
sentences.zh: 人们像阴沟里的狗一样生活。

sentences.en: Give a medieval churchman a science kit and you'd be roasting on the bonfire before you knew it.
sentences.zh: 给中世纪的教士一套科学工具，你还没反应过来，自己就已经在火刑柱上被烤了。

sentences.en: So Tom Holland, you can't surely disagree with such a nuanced account of the history of science, can you?
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆·霍兰，你肯定不会不同意这种对科学史如此细致入微的描述吧？

sentences.en: Dominic, I feel like walking off this podcast right now.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我现在就想退出这个播客。

sentences.en: I've never heard such nonsense.
sentences.zh: 我从未听过如此荒谬的言论。

sentences.en: The best thing about it is that yesterday you sent me an introduction.
sentences.zh: 最棒的是，昨天你还给我发了一篇介绍。

sentences.en: That you'd written yourself for me to use, quoting from one of your own essays.
sentences.zh: 那是你自己写好让我用的，还引用了你自己的一篇文章。

sentences.en: And I just refused to use it.
sentences.zh: 而我只是拒绝使用它。

sentences.en: It's from Dominion.
sentences.zh: 那是出自《多米尼恩》一书。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a fantastic passage.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是一段精彩的文字。

sentences.en: And I just refused to use it on principle.
sentences.zh: 我只是原则上拒绝使用它。

sentences.en: I know you did.
sentences.zh: 我知道你拒绝了。

sentences.en: It's against the spirit of the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这违背了播客的精神。

sentences.en: Oh, what?
sentences.zh: 哦，什么？

sentences.en: Promoting our books is against the spirit of the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 宣传我们的书违背了播客的精神。

sentences.en: Promoting your books is against the spirit of my podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 宣传你的书违背了我这个播客的精神。

sentences.en: So already, so I thought that, you know, I thought that that opening thing was the most ludicrous thing you could possibly have said.
sentences.zh: 所以，我已经……我觉得那段开场白简直是你所能说出的最荒谬的话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, obviously, I was setting it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很明显，我是在铺垫。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Yes, I know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So, OK, so today's topic is, we're titling it the medieval science.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那么今天的主题，我们将其定名为“中世纪科学”。

sentences.en: And we need a top historian.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一位顶尖的历史学家。

sentences.en: We always need a top historian.
sentences.zh: 我们总是需要一位顶尖的历史学家。

sentences.en: Medieval science.
sentences.zh: 中世纪科学。

sentences.en: And you, in your introduction, were kind of casting the Middle Ages as a dark age.
sentences.zh: 而你在介绍中，似乎把中世纪描绘成了一个黑暗时代。

sentences.en: Obscurantism.
sentences.zh: 蒙昧主义。

sentences.en: Yes, obscurantism.
sentences.zh: 是的，蒙昧主义。

sentences.en: We need someone who's written a book called The Light Ages.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一位写过《光明时代》这本书的人。

sentences.en: We do.
sentences.zh: 确实需要。

sentences.en: About how the Middle Ages was, far from being a period of ignorance and superstition,
sentences.zh: 关于中世纪远非一个无知和迷信的时期，

sentences.en: was kind of opened up all kinds of astonishing ways of seeing the world that we still benefit from today.
sentences.zh: 它实际上开启了各种令人惊叹的观察世界的方式，我们至今仍从中受益。

sentences.en: And that person is Seb Falk, author of The Light Ages, joining us from Cambridge, Seb, are you?
sentences.zh: 那个人就是塞布·福尔克，《光明时代》的作者，他正从剑桥连线我们，塞布，你在吗？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Hi, Seb.
sentences.zh: 你好，塞布。

sentences.en: Thanks for joining us.
sentences.zh: 感谢你加入我们。

sentences.en: So thanks so much for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你来参加节目。

sentences.en: And as I said, we're talking about medieval science.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，我们正在讨论中世纪科学。

sentences.en: And as you kind of tease out in your fabulous book, which I strongly recommend to anyone who's interested in this subject, even if you're not,
sentences.zh: 正如你在那本精彩的书中梳理的那样——我强烈向任何对这个主题感兴趣的人推荐这本书，即使你不感兴趣，

sentences.en: you'll find it incredibly interesting.
sentences.zh: 你也会发现它非常有趣。

sentences.en: You kind of say that both the words medieval and science are kind of tricky, that they imply slight degrees of anachronism.
sentences.zh: 你提到“中世纪”和“科学”这两个词都有点棘手，它们暗示了轻微的时代错误。

sentences.en: Could we just look at the word medieval first?
sentences.zh: 我们能先看看“中世纪”这个词吗？

sentences.en: Because it does still have a kind of slightly pejorative sense, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为它确实仍然带有一种轻微的贬义，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Medieval today is often used as a kind of synonym for backward or barbaric.
sentences.zh: 今天，“中世纪”常被用作落后或野蛮的同义词。

sentences.en: You know, we talk about those medieval Taliban or, you know, medieval lack of Wi-Fi in my favourite cafe.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们谈论那些“中世纪的塔利班”，或者我最喜欢的咖啡馆里“中世纪般的Wi-Fi缺失”。

sentences.en: And things that we do like, if they happen to happen between, let's say, the year 1000 and the year 1500, we call them something else.
sentences.zh: 而如果我们喜欢某些事物，如果它们恰好发生在，比如说公元1000年到1500年之间，我们就会给它们起别的名字。

sentences.en: We call them Renaissance or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为文艺复兴或其他什么。

sentences.en: But historically, the word medieval is already a bit of a way of dismissing the period, right?
sentences.zh: 但从历史上看，“中世纪”这个词本身就是一种否定该时期的方式，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it means the bit in the middle, the bit that's less interesting.
sentences.zh: 因为它意味着中间的那一段，那段不那么有趣的部分。

sentences.en: And that comes from the Renaissance, when they were trying to cast themselves as the heirs to ancient Greece and Rome.
sentences.zh: 这源于文艺复兴时期，当时他们试图将自己塑造为古希腊和罗马的继承者。

sentences.en: And they said that everything that had happened since the fall of Rome had been just an uninteresting bit in the middle.
sentences.zh: 他们说，自罗马陷落以来发生的一切都只是中间一段无趣的插曲。

sentences.en: So that history of medieval as being uninteresting and not worthy of consideration goes way back.
sentences.zh: 所以，将中世纪视为无趣且不值得考虑的历史观由来已久。

sentences.en: But I'm trying to rehabilitate it.
sentences.zh: 但我正在努力为它平反。

sentences.en: As you do brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 你做得非常出色。

sentences.en: And that sense of the Middle Ages as something backward obviously continues into the present.
sentences.zh: 而将中世纪视为落后时期的观念显然一直延续到了今天。

sentences.en: So we have a question from Tim O'Neill, on whose podcast I know you have appeared.
sentences.zh: 我们收到一个来自蒂姆·奥尼尔的问题，我知道你曾上过他的播客。

sentences.en: Indeed, I think you've appeared on almost every podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 确实，我想你几乎上过所有的播客。

sentences.en: And Tim, who runs a website called, what is it?
sentences.zh: 蒂姆经营着一个网站，叫什么来着？

sentences.en: History for Atheists.
sentences.zh: “无神论者的历史”。

sentences.en: And his kind of perspective is that atheists are as likely to believe nonsensical things about history as Christians or Muslims or whoever.
sentences.zh: 他的观点是，无神论者和基督徒、穆斯林或其他任何人一样，都有可能相信关于历史的荒谬言论。

sentences.en: And Tim asks, why is a period which gave us the optics that led to eyeglasses, the mechanics of complex astronomical clocks, logarithmic expression,
sentences.zh: 蒂姆问道，为什么一个为我们提供了制造眼镜的光学技术、复杂天文钟的机械原理、对数表达式、

sentences.en: the mean speed theorem and successful experiments in man flight depicted as a science free dark age?
sentences.zh: 平均速度定理以及人类飞行成功实验的时期，会被描绘成一个没有科学的黑暗时代？

sentences.en: And is it all the fault of people in the Renaissance saying that everything should be owed to the Renaissance?
sentences.zh: 这全是文艺复兴时期的人声称一切都应归功于文艺复兴的错吗？

sentences.en: Or does it go deeper than that?
sentences.zh: 还是说这背后有更深层的原因？

sentences.en: Slightly, it's also the fault of Protestants after the Reformation and sort of into the Enlightenment casting Catholics as superstitious and backward and witch burning.
sentences.zh: 稍微有一点，这也是宗教改革后的新教徒以及启蒙运动时期的人们的错，他们将天主教徒描绘成迷信、落后和焚烧女巫的人。

sentences.en: Actually, a lot of the stereotypes that are associated with the Middle Ages, like the burning of witches,
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多与中世纪相关的刻板印象，比如焚烧女巫，

sentences.en: are really more properly associated with the early modern period, or at least the beginning of the early modern period.
sentences.zh: 实际上更准确地说是与近代早期，或者至少是近代早期开始时相关联的。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's a bit of a bit of kind of Edward Gibbon talking about how people in in the Dark Ages were just following superstition.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，爱德华·吉本谈论黑暗时代的人们只是盲从迷信，这确实有点那种味道。

sentences.en: And some of that is a way of beating up the Catholics, essentially.
sentences.zh: 而其中一些本质上是为了打击天主教徒的一种手段。

sentences.en: And so if we then also look at the word science, I mean, science in the sense that we use it today.
sentences.zh: 那么，如果我们再看看“科学”这个词，我的意思是，我们今天所使用的“科学”这个词。

sentences.en: That's quite late, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这出现得很晚，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, basically, it's kind of the word scientist we only get in the 19th century, mid 19th century in Oxford.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上，“科学家”这个词直到19世纪，即19世纪中叶的牛津才出现。

sentences.en: The word science is kind of being used to describe the works of Aristotle or Greek philosophy or a whole range of things.
sentences.zh: “科学”这个词曾被用来描述亚里士多德的著作、希腊哲学或一系列其他事物。

sentences.en: So the idea of science that we have now, I mean, where does that come from?
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在所拥有的科学概念，到底是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: And to what extent does it kind of, our use of it kind of get in the way of our understanding what people in the Middle Ages are doing?
sentences.zh: 我们在多大程度上因为使用这个词而阻碍了对中世纪人们所作所为的理解？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's absolutely part of the problem, that the idea of a kind of modern science that's practiced by professionals in purpose-designed spaces with, you know,
sentences.zh: 是的，这绝对是问题的一部分，即由专业人士在专门设计的空间里，使用，你知道，

sentences.en: very specific and expensive equipment is a modern concept.
sentences.zh: 非常具体且昂贵的设备所实践的现代科学概念，是一个现代概念。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that people weren't kind of looking around themselves and wondering about the universe,
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着人们没有在观察周围并对宇宙感到好奇，

sentences.en: but they might have been doing it in different ways and for different reasons.
sentences.zh: 只是他们可能以不同的方式、出于不同的原因在做这件事。

sentences.en: And I think part of the problem is that we assume that there's only one way of doing science.
sentences.zh: 我认为问题的一部分在于我们假设只有一种做科学的方法。

sentences.en: There's only one reason to do science.
sentences.zh: 做科学只有一个理由。

sentences.en: But even if you actually look at modern science today, there are different motivations.
sentences.zh: 但即使你审视今天的现代科学，也会发现有不同的动机。

sentences.en: Are you trying to understand the universe in a disinterested way, purely for the pleasure of finding things out?
sentences.zh: 你是为了以一种超然的方式理解宇宙，纯粹是为了发现事物的乐趣吗？

sentences.en: Or are you trying to improve people's lives?
sentences.zh: 还是为了改善人们的生活？

sentences.en: And those are two potentially conflicting motivations for doing science.
sentences.zh: 这两者是做科学时可能存在冲突的动机。

sentences.en: And in the Middle Ages, a lot of the motivations for doing science or for trying to understand the universe are for things that turn out to be somewhat misguided, perhaps,
sentences.zh: 而在中世纪，许多做科学或试图理解宇宙的动机，可能被证明在某种程度上是误导的，

sentences.en: or that many people today would say are wrong, trying to understand God's universe from the point of view of religious people,
sentences.zh: 或者许多现代人会说那是错误的；从宗教人士的角度去理解上帝的宇宙，

sentences.en: many atheists today would say is completely pointless,
sentences.zh: 许多现代无神论者会说这是完全毫无意义的，

sentences.en: or trying to understand the motions of the planets in order to be able to provide an astrological cure for somebody's disease, again, would be thought to be slightly misguided.
sentences.zh: 或者为了能够为某人的疾病提供占星术治疗而试图理解行星的运动，同样会被认为有点误导。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that underneath those misguided motivations or overlaying those false premises isn't some really interesting methodology,
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着在那些被误导的动机之下，或者在那些错误的前提之上，不存在真正有趣的方法论，

sentences.en: some really interesting science, and some really fantastic ideas and measurements and instruments.
sentences.zh: 不存在真正有趣的科学，以及真正奇妙的想法、测量和仪器。

sentences.en: So, let's go back to the beginning of the period.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回到那个时期的开始。

sentences.en: So, somebody asked a question online, Humphrey Clark, he asked a question about Dan Jones' new history of the Middle Ages,
sentences.zh: 有人在网上提问，汉弗莱·克拉克，他问了一个关于丹·琼斯新著《中世纪史》的问题，

sentences.en: in which Dan Jones talks about the late Roman Empire and its Byzantine successor, kind of blocking knowledge by sort of shutting off classical learning.
sentences.zh: 丹·琼斯在书中谈到晚期罗马帝国及其拜占庭继承者，通过切断古典学习来阻碍知识传播。

sentences.en: Do you think that's true?
sentences.zh: 你认为这是真的吗？

sentences.en: Is there a period at the end of the Roman Empire, in the beginning of what we'd call the Middle Ages,
sentences.zh: 在罗马帝国末期，在我们所称的中世纪初期，是否存在一个时期，

sentences.en: is when people almost deliberately turn their backs on what we would now call the scientific learning of the classical era,
sentences.zh: 人们几乎是有意地背弃了我们现在所称的古典时代的科学知识，

sentences.en: or does that learning sort of continue unbroken, as it were?
sentences.zh: 还是说这种知识在某种程度上是未曾中断地延续了下来？

sentences.en: I mean, there are cases of church fathers saying, you know, you don't need to worry about this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有教会神父说，你知道，你不需要担心这些东西。

sentences.en: There's a very famous quotation, which is, I think, often misinterpreted by Tertullian, saying, you know, what does Athens have to do with Jerusalem?
sentences.zh: 有一个非常著名的引言，我想经常被误解，来自特土良，他说，你知道，雅典与耶路撒冷有什么关系？

sentences.en: In other words, and I'm sure Tom would weigh in on this.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我相信汤姆会对此发表意见。

sentences.en: I'm itching, too, but I'm going to restrain myself.
sentences.zh: 我确实很想说，但我会克制自己。

sentences.en: But I think there's equally church fathers like St Augustine, who says, you know, knowledge, pagan knowledge is like the Egyptian gold that the Israelites stole out of Egypt,
sentences.zh: 但我认为同样有像圣奥古斯丁这样的教会神父，他说，你知道，知识，异教知识就像以色列人从埃及偷走的埃及黄金，

sentences.en: except it wasn't stealing because they were putting it to better use.
sentences.zh: 只不过那不是偷窃，因为他们是在更好地利用它。

sentences.en: And so pagan knowledge, in the same way, could be put to better use by Christians.
sentences.zh: 因此，异教知识同样可以被基督徒更好地利用。

sentences.en: So, you know, there's always arguments and differences of opinion.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，总是有争论和意见分歧。

sentences.en: If there was a period of kind of intellectual stagnation, it was, I would say, more structural.
sentences.zh: 如果说存在一个智力停滞的时期，我会说，那更多是结构性的。

sentences.en: It was about economic decline that follows the decline of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 这是罗马帝国衰落后随之而来的经济衰退。

sentences.en: And therefore, networks of communication, systems of knowledge production were all destroyed and decaying.
sentences.zh: 因此，通信网络、知识生产系统都遭到破坏并走向衰落。

sentences.en: And so it was harder for information to be shared.
sentences.zh: 所以信息共享变得更加困难。

sentences.en: But let's not forget that the Roman Empire continues in Byzantium and knowledge continues to be spread and communicated.
sentences.zh: 但别忘了，罗马帝国在拜占庭延续了下来，知识继续传播和交流。

sentences.en: And then, of course, translated from Greek into Syriac and from Syriac into Arabic.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，从希腊语翻译成叙利亚语，再从叙利亚语翻译成阿拉伯语。

sentences.en: And, you know, the centers of knowledge are perhaps passed to the Islamic world.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，知识中心也许转移到了伊斯兰世界。

sentences.en: So, you know, I don't think there's ever really a period when you can say that people were uninterested in knowing stuff about the world.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我不认为有任何时期你可以说人们对了解世界不感兴趣。

sentences.en: People's motivations change and people's ability to protect and preserve and communicate and build on ancient knowledge had its peaks and troughs.
sentences.zh: 人们的动机在改变，人们保护、保存、交流和建立在古代知识之上的能力也有起有落。

sentences.en: But I think to cast the whole period as a period in which people just didn't want to know anything is a modern stereotype,
sentences.zh: 但我认为将整个时期描绘成一个人们根本不想知道任何事情的时期，是一个现代的刻板印象，

sentences.en: basically based on kind of our own prejudices about the past, because they don't look like us and they don't think like us.
sentences.zh: 基本上是基于我们自己对过去的偏见，因为他们看起来不像我们，想得也不像我们。

sentences.en: And, Seb, isn't it also, I mean, just to go back to this thing about how science is a recent coinage, really.
sentences.zh: 而且，塞布，难道不是吗？我的意思是，回到科学是一个近期创造的词这件事上。

sentences.en: And basically what science comes to mean in the 19th century is something that's not religion.
sentences.zh: 基本上，科学在19世纪所指的就是非宗教的东西。

sentences.en: And likewise, religion comes to mean something that's not science.
sentences.zh: 同样，宗教也开始指代非科学的东西。

sentences.en: And the two are kind of separated out.
sentences.zh: 两者被分开了。

sentences.en: But before that, it was always accepted that the attempt to understand the universe and to fathom its workings and to explain it in ways that perhaps today we would cast a science.

sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《历史的其余部分》。

sentences.en: Uh, Tom Holland has indeed been thinking about the clock in Salisbury and I have indeed made the cosmos in a box, which is testimony to my power.
sentences.zh: 嗯，汤姆·霍兰确实一直在思考索尔兹伯里的时钟，而我也确实在一个盒子里重现了宇宙，这证明了我的能力。

sentences.en: Now, Seb Falk is with us and he's talking about medieval science.
sentences.zh: 现在，塞布·福克和我们在一起，他要谈谈中世纪科学。

sentences.en: And before the break, we were talking about clocks and, and tinkering and the extent to which people, you know, were doing, I suppose, what we would very loosely now call science.
sentences.zh: 在休息之前，我们谈到了时钟和修补，以及人们在多大程度上，你知道，在做我们现在可以非常宽泛地称为科学的事情。

sentences.en: My question, Seb, is about progress.
sentences.zh: 塞布，我的问题是关于进步的。

sentences.en: So obviously so much of our sense of a scientific narrative is based on the idea of progress,
sentences.zh: 显然，我们对科学叙事的很多理解都基于进步的理念，

sentences.en: of standing on the shoulders of giants, which we alluded to before, and building something bigger and bigger every time.
sentences.zh: 即我们之前提到的“站在巨人的肩膀上”，并且每次都构建出更宏大的东西。

sentences.en: So you have Newton and then you have his successors and so on and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以你有牛顿，然后有他的继任者，以此类推。

sentences.en: You get to Einstein.
sentences.zh: 一直到爱因斯坦。

sentences.en: That's the story.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个故事。

sentences.en: You know, it is a story.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这确实是一个故事。

sentences.en: Did they have a sense of something like that?
sentences.zh: 他们有类似这样的意识吗？

sentences.en: Did they have any sense of there being a progressive narrative towards greater enlightenment, as it were?
sentences.zh: 他们是否意识到存在一种通向更伟大启蒙的进步叙事？

sentences.en: The short answer is no, because according to the Christian story, everything was declined after the Garden of Eden, basically.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：没有。因为根据基督教的故事，伊甸园之后的一切基本上都在衰落。

sentences.en: And so if you asked a Christian scholar, they would say that what they were trying to do was
sentences.zh: 所以如果你问一位基督教学者，他们会说他们试图做的是

sentences.en: to preserve ancient knowledge and to build on it and to try and redefine it and to try and understand it.
sentences.zh: 保存古代知识，在此基础上进行构建，尝试重新定义它并试图理解它。

sentences.en: But the sense that they had a lot of the time was that they would never be able to reclaim the perfect wisdom of the Garden of Eden.
sentences.zh: 但他们很多时候的感觉是，他们永远无法找回伊甸园中那种完美的智慧。

sentences.en: So in that story of the fall, there is a sort of complexity of, well, we couldn't be where we are without it, and yet we will never be able to sort of go back to that perfect time.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个堕落的故事中，有一种复杂性，即“没有它我们就不会有今天”，但同时“我们永远无法回到那个完美的时代”。

sentences.en: So they didn't have a sense that they were making perfect progress.
sentences.zh: 所以他们并没有认为自己在取得完美的进步。

sentences.en: But that didn't mean that in practical terms, they couldn't learn things and they couldn't discover new things and they couldn't find out what other people knew.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着在实践层面，他们不能学习新事物、发现新事物，或者了解别人所知道的东西。

sentences.en: But the part of the problem with progress also is that it depends on what you define as progress and what counts as progress.
sentences.zh: 但进步问题的一部分还在于，这取决于你如何定义进步，以及什么才算进步。

sentences.en: So they might have thought about progress in moral terms and, you know, how can we become better people and how can we know God better?
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能从道德层面思考进步，你知道，我们如何才能成为更好的人，我们如何才能更好地认识上帝？

sentences.en: And that was something that they could perhaps achieve in their own minds.
sentences.zh: 这在他们自己的心目中或许是可以实现的。

sentences.en: So I think part of the problem is that we assume that we all agree on what progress is and that humanity must make some sort of linear progression.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为问题的一部分在于，我们假设大家都同意什么是进步，并且人类必须进行某种线性的演进。

sentences.en: And that isn't the case in history in the sense of, well, sometimes knowledge has gone backwards and also we haven't always agreed on what counts as progress to begin with.
sentences.zh: 但在历史上并非如此，因为有时知识会倒退，而且我们对于什么才算进步也并非总是达成一致。

sentences.en: But we define progress, don't we, very much as mastery over nature.
sentences.zh: 但我们定义进步，不是吗，很大程度上将其定义为对自然的掌控。

sentences.en: You know, we can transcend the limits of the natural world, but they presumably didn't have a sense of that in the same way.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们可以超越自然世界的限制，但他们大概没有以同样的方式意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Well, certainly their nature was one in which God intervened on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，他们的自然观是上帝每天都会干预其中的那种。

sentences.en: And so there were limitations to what humans could know and what humans could do.
sentences.zh: 所以人类能知道什么、能做什么是有局限性的。

sentences.en: And I think it's very important, I suppose, to emphasise that they wanted to be modest about
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，强调他们对自然保持谦逊是非常重要的，

sentences.en: about nature in the sense of, well, in some sense it wasn't really for humans to try and be gods, essentially, to set themselves up as gods.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种意义上，人类本质上并不应该试图成为上帝，不应该把自己摆在上帝的位置上。

sentences.en: But they have a spark of the divine reason, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但他们拥有神圣理性的火花，不是吗？

sentences.en: The lux hominem.
sentences.zh: 即“人类之光”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it is a tension.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种张力。

sentences.en: It is a tension.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一种张力。

sentences.en: I think one of the things that we have to get away from is this idea that medieval people agreed about everything and constantly behaved in a consistent way.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须摒弃的一种观念是：中世纪的人们对所有事情都达成一致，并且行为始终保持一致。

sentences.en: Neither of those things are true.
sentences.zh: 这两点都不是事实。

sentences.en: So they can say we have to be modest in our ambitions to understand God because we could never understand God and it would be blasphemous even to think that we could, yet appearing
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以说，我们必须在理解上帝的野心上保持谦逊，因为我们永远无法理解上帝，甚至认为我们可以理解上帝都是亵渎，然而在

sentences.en: in all of their actions that they spent all of their time trying to understand God and trying
sentences.zh: 他们所有的行动中，似乎又花费了所有时间试图去理解上帝，并试图

sentences.en: to understand God through nature, which was, you know, a very clear principle of something that could be done.
sentences.zh: 通过自然去理解上帝，这显然是一个可以做到的明确原则。

sentences.en: So, you know, there are contradictions there.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这里面存在矛盾。

sentences.en: And so also, do you think, I mean, do you think the Christian idea of God is that he's all-powerful, that he's created everything?
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为，我的意思是，你认为基督教对上帝的看法是全能的、创造了一切吗？

sentences.en: So there is the sense of the universe as a kind of a coherent entity that perhaps in other ways of understanding the cosmos you don't necessarily get.
sentences.zh: 所以有一种将宇宙视为一个连贯实体的感觉，这在其他理解宇宙的方式中未必能得到。

sentences.en: And on top of that, Christianity has this idea that God subjects himself to covenants.
sentences.zh: 而且除此之外，基督教还有一种上帝使自己服从于契约的观念。

sentences.en: So he has a covenant with Moses, you know, he kind of signs up to that.
sentences.zh: 所以他与摩西有契约，你知道，他算是签署了那个契约。

sentences.en: And whatever exactly it is, the crucifixion, you know, what's going on there, there is a sense that in some way there's some kind of agreement that's being drawn up.
sentences.zh: 无论具体是什么，比如受难，你知道，那里发生了什么，有一种感觉是，在某种程度上达成了一种协议。

sentences.en: So do you think that that implies that both that God is all-powerful, but that he is happy to construct laws that perhaps humans can fathom?
sentences.zh: 所以你认为这是否意味着上帝既是全能的，又乐于制定人类或许可以理解的法律？

sentences.en: And that therefore there's a kind of theological framework for what we would now see as, you know, the attempt to work out laws that underpin the running of the universe?
sentences.zh: 因此，对于我们现在所看到的，即试图找出支撑宇宙运行的规律，是否存在一种神学框架？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And there is even a tension there though, right?
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，这里面也存在一种张力，对吧？

sentences.en: Because the physicists, you know, followers of Aristotle try to understand the universe in the terms in which Aristotle put it and
sentences.zh: 因为物理学家，你知道，亚里士多德的追随者，试图用亚里士多德提出的术语来理解宇宙，并

sentences.en: try and explain kind of what is and isn't possible according to the laws of physics.
sentences.zh: 试图解释根据物理定律什么是可能的，什么是不可能的。

sentences.en: And that to us makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 这对我们来说很有意义。

sentences.en: But if you talk about the laws of physics, then the theologians might get a little bit tense and antsy about constraining the power of God.

sentences.en: And, and, and he's drawing on, on stuff from Central Asia.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且，而且他正在利用来自中亚的东西。

sentences.en: I mean, yes.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的。

sentences.en: I mean, well you, you, yes and no.
sentences.zh: 我是说，好吧，你，你，既是也不是。

sentences.en: So, uh, the, the ideas that the earth might be, um, going around the sun rather than the reverse, um, is, is found in, uh, ancient European sources.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，地球可能，嗯，绕着太阳转而不是相反的想法，嗯，是在，嗯，古代欧洲文献中发现的。

sentences.en: It's found in, um, Roman and, and, and Greek sources.
sentences.zh: 它是在，嗯，罗马和，和，和希腊文献中发现的。

sentences.en: It's suggested, uh, and Copernicus goes back to those, a true Renaissance man, that he's going back to the classical sources to try to, uh,
sentences.zh: 它被提出，嗯，哥白尼回到了那些，一个真正的文艺复兴人，他回到古典文献中试图，嗯，

sentences.en: find other people who have thought what he thinks in the past as a kind of support for his assumptions.
sentences.zh: 寻找过去也持有他这种想法的人，作为对他假设的一种支持。

sentences.en: So in that sense, he's a true medieval.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，他是一个真正的中世纪人。

sentences.en: He's trying to look for authorities to back up his ideas.
sentences.zh: 他试图寻找权威来支持他的想法。

sentences.en: Um, the geometry that he uses to make it work, that comes from the Islamic world, that comes from Central Asia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他用来使其运作的几何学，来自伊斯兰世界，来自中亚。

sentences.en: Um, and so he draws on a, a, a bunch of, um, scholars, most notably Atusi, uh, who was Persian in the, in the 14th century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以他利用了一群，嗯，学者，最著名的是图西，嗯，他是14世纪的波斯人。

sentences.en: Oh, Ali, I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 哦，阿里，我很抱歉。

sentences.en: I would be thrilled to hear that.
sentences.zh: 听到这个我会很激动。

sentences.en: It's, it's, it's, it's all Persian.
sentences.zh: 这，这，这，这全是波斯的。

sentences.en: Well, there's, there's a whole bunch of them, Al-Urdia, Shirazi, or, you know, from, from, from across the Islamic world.
sentences.zh: 好吧，有，有一大群人，阿尔-乌尔迪，设拉子，或者，你知道，来自，来自，来自整个伊斯兰世界。

sentences.en: Um, and it, it's argued still by historians how much Copernicus depends on them versus independently discovering these geometrical models.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，历史学家们仍在争论哥白尼在多大程度上依赖他们，而不是独立发现这些几何模型。

sentences.en: But he basically has to
sentences.zh: 但他基本上必须

sentences.en: answer with this idea.
sentences.zh: 用这个想法来回答。

sentences.en: Well, he thinks that actually it's the sun that's at the center of the universe, not the earth.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他认为实际上是太阳处于宇宙中心，而不是地球。

sentences.en: Uh, he sticks to the idea of perfect circles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他坚持完美圆形的想法。

sentences.en: So he can't make it work because, uh, the universe doesn't operate in perfect circles, but Copernicus, uh, maintains this,
sentences.zh: 所以他无法使其运作，因为，嗯，宇宙并不是以完美的圆形运行的，但哥白尼，嗯，坚持这个，

sentences.en: uh, basic principle that motion in the heavens should be in, in perfect circles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本原则，即天体的运动应该是，嗯，完美的圆形。

sentences.en: And so he ends up with a system that is basically just as complicated as the one that he started with, but replaces, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以他最终得到的系统基本上和他开始时一样复杂，但替换了，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it's, it's, it's not just as complicated, but it's also as unprovable.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它，它，它不仅一样复杂，而且同样无法证明。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And there are clear objections to Copernicus's theories.
sentences.zh: 而且对哥白尼的理论有明显的反对意见。

sentences.en: Uh, most obviously the fact that if we're moving through the universe at thousands of miles an hour, why do we not feel the wind rushing past our ears?
sentences.zh: 嗯，最明显的事实是，如果我们以每小时数千英里的速度在宇宙中穿行，为什么我们感觉不到风从耳边掠过？

sentences.en: Um, and if, uh, we are moving thousands of miles in the course of a year, uh, why do we, uh, not observe any parallax in the stars?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且如果，嗯，我们在一年中移动了数千英里，嗯，为什么我们，嗯，没有观察到恒星的任何视差？

sentences.en: Uh, and those questions weren't resolved, um, for a long time after Copernicus was, was writing in the early 16th century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些问题在哥白尼于16世纪初写作后的很长一段时间内都没有得到解决。

sentences.en: Uh, so there were objections to him at the time, those objections were voiced, you know, very clearly by scholars who were, you know, equally, if not more eminent than him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以当时有人反对他，那些反对意见，你知道，被那些，你知道，同样，如果不是比他更杰出的学者非常清楚地表达了出来。

sentences.en: Um, and other models were proposed, most notably, uh, that of, um, Tycho Brahe in, in Denmark, who proposed, uh, that essentially all the planets went
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且还提出了其他模型，最著名的是，嗯，丹麦的第谷·布拉赫的模型，他提出，嗯，本质上所有的行星都绕着

sentences.en: around the sun, uh, except the earth, uh, the sun goes around the earth.
sentences.zh: 太阳转，嗯，除了地球，嗯，太阳绕着地球转。

sentences.en: So that also, uh, in fact, that explains the phenomena that we observe better than Copernicus's model.
sentences.zh: 所以这也，嗯，事实上，这比哥白尼的模型更好地解释了我们观察到的现象。

sentences.en: So what we see in the 16th century is this constant argument, this back and forth, and that is the, the basis of science, really.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在16世纪看到的是这种不断的争论，这种来回，而这确实是科学的基础。

sentences.en: It's the argument, not this idea of, you know, some great person coming up with the right answer and everybody else immediately falls into line.
sentences.zh: 这是争论，而不是那种，你知道，某个伟人想出了正确答案，然后其他人立即跟进的想法。

sentences.en: Seb, is this the point where medieval science, as it were, is coming to an end and we're moving into some new phase?
sentences.zh: 塞布，这是中世纪科学即将结束，我们正在进入某个新阶段的时刻吗？

sentences.en: So obviously, you know, our sense of time is, much as we like to complicate it, we do divide it into kind of blocks.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，你知道，我们对时间的感知，尽管我们喜欢把它复杂化，但我们确实把它分成了若干块。

sentences.en: Is this the sort of 15th century Copernicus and then getting into the, the sort of early modern period, is that a definite shift as you see it in our scientific history?
sentences.zh: 这是15世纪的哥白尼，然后进入，嗯，某种早期现代时期，在你看来，这是我们科学史上明确的转变吗？

sentences.en: Well, there definitely is a change that takes place, but it's very gradual.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实发生了变化，但它是非常渐进的。

sentences.en: And, and most people would sort of put it in the 17th century, sometime between Galileo and Kepler and, uh, the end of Newton's career at the beginning of the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 而且，而且大多数人会把它放在17世纪，在伽利略和开普勒之间，以及，嗯，牛顿职业生涯结束到18世纪初之间的某个时间。

sentences.en: Um, what we see in Copernicus is, is definitely a shift because he's taking advantage of the new medium of printing, uh, to exchange ideas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在哥白尼身上看到的，绝对是一个转变，因为他利用了印刷术这一新媒介，嗯，来交流思想。

sentences.en: Uh, and, um, but, but, but he also, you know, as I already said, uh, in, in his kind of looking back to earlier authorities, uh, is, is a real
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，嗯，但是，但是，但是他也，你知道，正如我已经说过的，嗯，在他那种回顾早期权威的方式中，嗯，是一个真正的

sentences.en: Renaissance man.
sentences.zh: 文艺复兴人。

sentences.en: And, and his, uh, De Revolutionibus, his, his book in which he presents his heliocentric
sentences.zh: 而且，而且他的，嗯，《天体运行论》，他的，他的书，他在其中提出了他的日心

sentences.en: theory is modeled very closely on Ptolemy's AlmageSt. So, uh, he is, uh, self-consciously presenting himself in some sense as medieval.
sentences.zh: 理论，非常紧密地模仿了托勒密的《大成》。所以，嗯，他，嗯，自觉地在某种意义上把自己表现为中世纪人。

sentences.en: Um, but that's a sensible way to promote your ideas really, because if you want people to, you know, take something controversial and, and understand it, you have to
sentences.zh: 嗯，但这确实是一种推广你想法的明智方式，因为如果你想让人们，你知道，接受一些有争议的东西，并且，并且理解它，你必须

sentences.en: present it in terms that they're going to accept.
sentences.zh: 以他们会接受的术语来呈现它。

sentences.en: Um, what we see later is, is a whole shift in, in ideas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们后来看到的是，嗯，思想上的全面转变。

sentences.en: And, and part of that is a kind of valorization of the new and original, um, which
sentences.zh: 而且，而且其中一部分是对新事物和原创性的一种推崇，嗯，这

sentences.en: some people have associated with, uh, the European discovery of what they call the new world, um, as,
sentences.zh: 有些人将其与，嗯，欧洲人发现他们所谓的新世界联系起来，嗯，作为，

sentences.en: as a kind of way of proving that actually something new, we can know something new that the ancients didn't know about.
sentences.zh: 作为一种证明，实际上有新的东西，我们可以知道一些古人不知道的新东西。

sentences.en: Um, but also there's a kind of increase in experimentation and increase in, uh, inductive knowledge, uh, observing nature and not worrying too much about whether your
sentences.zh: 嗯，但实验也在增加，归纳知识也在增加，嗯，观察自然，而不必太担心你的

sentences.en: observations were the same as what somebody else might observe, which was always a stumbling
sentences.zh: 观察结果是否与别人可能观察到的相同，这在中世纪一直是一个绊脚石，

sentences.en: block in the middle ages, this idea that our senses were fallible and therefore we couldn't rely too much on our own observations.
sentences.zh: 这种认为我们的感官是不可靠的，因此我们不能太依赖我们自己的观察的想法。

sentences.en: But you could say, couldn't you, that, you know, this process of experimentation, that some of the areas that we now regard as, as absolutely not science,
sentences.zh: 但你可以说，不是吗，这种实验的过程，我们现在认为绝对不是科学的一些领域，

sentences.en: say astrology or alchemy or whatever, that that is, you know, testing to find out whether they work or not is a process of experimentation.
sentences.zh: 比如占星术或炼金术等等，那，你知道，测试以找出它们是否有效，是一个实验的过程。

sentences.en: And that in a sense, the kind of line that becomes by the 19th century, what we would now call science.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种意义上，这种路线到了19世纪，就成了我们现在所说的科学。

sentences.en: I mean, that, that we arrive at that through a process of, of, of testing other approaches to knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那，那是我们通过测试其他知识方法的过程而达到的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's all about how systematic it is, right?
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于它有多系统，对吧？

sentences.en: Because experimentum in Latin just means experience.
sentences.zh: 因为拉丁语中的“experimentum”只是意味着经验。

sentences.en: It just means something that, that happens to you.
sentences.zh: 它只是意味着某件，嗯，发生在你身上的事情。

sentences.en: Uh, and so this process of, of experiment morphing into something that is, uh, a discrete moment in time and to something that you design, something that you carry out and you
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这个过程，嗯，实验演变成某种，嗯，时间上的离散时刻，以及你设计的东西，你执行的东西，你

sentences.en: might do multiple times in order to check it.
sentences.zh: 可能会多次做以检查它。

sentences.en: That's, uh, something that happens gradually over time from this medieval idea that experiment is just an experience that you had that maybe happened
sentences.zh: 那是，嗯，随着时间的推移逐渐发生的事情，从这种中世纪的观点来看，实验只是你拥有的一种经验，也许发生了

sentences.en: to you rather than something that you did.
sentences.zh: 在你身上，而不是你做的事情。

sentences.en: So we can't really ever say one person invented experiment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真的不能说某个人发明了实验。

sentences.en: It's an idea that evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 这是一个随着时间推移而演变的想法。

sentences.en: But basically we could say, I mean, just to kind of draw a line onto it, we could say monks, yay for monks.
sentences.zh: 但基本上我们可以说，我是说，只是为了给它划一条线，我们可以说僧侣，为僧侣欢呼。

sentences.en: Well, they're experienced.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们很有经验。

sentences.en: They're not the baddies.
sentences.zh: 他们不是坏人。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole point, the whole point about, uh, Copernicus, right, is that he is a sort of
sentences.zh: 我是说，关于，嗯，哥白尼的全部重点，对吧，是他是一种

sentences.en: symptom of, uh, an increase in knowledge that the universe is not operating as we want it to, to do.
sentences.zh: 知识增加的症状，即宇宙并没有按照我们想要它做的方式运行。

sentences.en: Uh, and so astronomers over centuries noticed that the models of Ptolemy didn't quite match up to reality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以几个世纪以来的天文学家注意到托勒密模型与现实并不完全吻合。

sentences.en: It was just a kind of question of how content they were with the imperfection.
sentences.zh: 这只是他们对不完美有多大程度的满足感的问题。

sentences.en: And it's, it's an increase in, in experience.
sentences.zh: 而且，这是，这是经验的增加。

sentences.en: It's an increase in calculation.
sentences.zh: 这是计算的增加。

sentences.en: It's an increase in all the things that medieval people did that allows them to say, you know, this isn't good enough.
sentences.zh: 这是中世纪人所做的一切事情的增加，这使他们能够说，你知道，这还不够好。

sentences.en: We need a better system.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个更好的系统。

sentences.en: Uh, so it relies on that medieval practice, even if it takes a little bit longer for somebody to come up with an alternative that works better.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以它依赖于那种中世纪的实践，即使有人想出更好的替代方案需要更长的时间。

sentences.en: Brilliant.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Um, and, uh, and your book, The Light Ages, is great.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且，嗯，而且你的书，《光明时代》，很棒。

sentences.en: I, I read it in proof and then I read it again yesterday to prepare for this and I enjoyed it just as much the second time as the firSt. So thank you and buy it guys.
sentences.zh: 我，我读了校样，昨天为了准备这个又读了一遍，第二次读和第一次读一样享受。所以谢谢你，大家去买吧。

sentences.en: Cause it bears definitely a second reading.
sentences.zh: 因为它绝对值得二读。

sentences.en: Uh, thanks so much, Seb.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常感谢，塞布。

sentences.en: Thanks everyone to listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: We will be back soon with, what are we going to be doing?
sentences.zh: 我们很快会回来，我们要去做什么来着？

sentences.en: We don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们也不知道。

sentences.en: We haven't decided yet.
sentences.zh: 还没定呢。

sentences.en: Something, something experimental process.
sentences.zh: 总之，某种实验性的过程吧。

sentences.en: We, we, yeah, we need to, we need to work that out.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们，对，我们需要，我们需要把这事儿定下来。

sentences.en: Um, thanks very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 嗯，非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: See you all soon.
sentences.zh: 很快再见。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 感谢收听《历史余音》。
